name: clawd

sheet.role: the source design (idol_D): the input to the generated references, and no measure's authority (Michael, 2026-09-28: drawn in another aesthetic and scale than the turnarounds). The authority map's 'sheet' role is filled by the generated sheets (the manifest's 'sheets': face, eyes, body)

scale.method: its front figure's height against the rig's (the same drawing at a known scale)

cautions: low resolution (a head is about 115 px per head length): eye-spacing scale is +-4%, use the figure height

rig.role: the front design at high resolution, cut into layers: eye layers (the eyes' shape, iris, pupil), the face layer, hair layers

scale.method: eye layers' spacing = 2 * eye_x head lengths

cautions: the face layer is bled out under the hair (about 15 px): its bottom is not the chin; take the chin from the sheet

key3d.role: a 3D-style restyle of the design (front, full body): the TRELLIS input and the ref_iou silhouette
cautions: an interpretation of the design, not the design: its face is rounder and fuller than the sheet's

trellis.role: the 3D target: the hair's shape, the face's depth where the drawings have none, the silhouette per band

provenance.note: the command is reconstructed from the output's name and the run's settings, not logged at the time

cautions: 48 MB, kept out of git: regenerate with the command, or copy it into charkit/out/i3d/clawd/

outfit_graph.role: the outfit as pieces: types, sides and mirror pairs, attachments (bone, parent), layer order, colours, extents per sheet view and in 3D, motion classes with reasons, template mapping and spring chains
cautions: measured from the rig, the sheet and the generated field, cross-checked with the annotated vision pass (outfit_notes.json): read its flags before trusting a piece

head_turnaround.role: the head at about 4x the sheet's resolution: front, 3/4 (left), true profile (left), back at one scale; the profile shows the eye set back, the pointed nose, lips, chin and jaw
cautions: a generated interpretation of the design: check it against the sheet (silhouettes and landmarks at the sheet's scale) before letting it grade anything

head_construction.role: the bald head with construction lines (skull top, brow, eye line, nose, mouth, chin), front and profile: the skull and the face shape under the hair, the ear, the eye's set-back in profile; also the eye close-up: its front eye is ~1.6x the rig's eye layer and measures the same with charkit.eyeqa (opening aspect 0.922 vs 0.925, iris ratio 0.59 vs 0.61, pupil share of the iris 0.067 vs 0.071)
cautions: a generated interpretation: its front chin is more pointed than the sheet's; trust it for the profile and the skull, check the front against the sheet

garment_breakdown.role: the outfit as a labelled flat-lay of its pieces: bodice front and back, puff sleeves, sailor collar, bow with tails, outer skirt, cream front panel, stepped back panels L/R, shorts, wrist cuffs, boots front and back
cautions: flat-lay scale is not body scale: use it for piece shapes, counts (pleats, hem steps) and the piece list, not for sizes on the body

hair_breakdown.role: the hair as colour-coded layers in front, profile and back (bangs, side locks, upper and lower back, buns, ahoge, flyaways) with a legend: a machine-readable layer map for the hair components
cautions: layer families are reliable; individual locks within a family are only partly separated (close shades)

sleeve_closeup.role: the puff sleeve's construction on a mannequin arm, front, outer side and back: the gathered sleeve cap at the armhole, the balloon volume, the gathers into the cream band above the elbow; a cross-section at the widest point (how far the fabric stands off the arm all round); the wrist cuff front and side with its stepped notch
cautions: the mannequin is generic, not Clawd's body: use it for the sleeve's shape, gathers and stand-off relative to the arm, and take the puff's size on the body from the sheet

skirt_closeup.role: the layered skirt's construction on a mannequin, front, side profile and back, plus a top-down view of the panel order round the waist: the knife-pleated orange outer skirt, the pleated cream front panel set into it, and the longer stepped zig-zag under-panels at the sides and back; the side view gives the hem flare and the longer back
cautions: the mannequin is generic: take the skirt's length and flare on the body from the sheet

the top-down view is schematic: it puts stepped edging on every outer panel, where the back view shows a plain outer hem over stepped under-panels; use it for panel order and count, check the hem against the sheet's views

body_turnaround.role: the full body for 3D modelling in one generation: front, three-quarter (turned to the viewer's left), true side profile (facing left) and back, one A-pose, one scale, one ground line and eye line, the complete outfit; the base for the body and hair silhouettes, the outfit's placement and the palette (Michael, 2026-09-28: idol_D is the source design, not a benchmark)
cautions: the arms hang about 20-25 degrees out from vertical, not the 45 asked for: the rest-pose knobs fit it
check it against the head sheets (charkit refcheck) before it grades anything

inputs: body_turnaround (edited in place: the sheet on a canvas widened by 1280 px of its grey)

body_turnaround_back34.role: two more full-body views of the body sheet's figure, drawn by extending body_turnaround itself (its four views kept: registered IoU 0.983-0.987, scale within 0.15%, eye and ground lines within 0.016 L): three-quarter backs from behind her left (5th figure) and right (6th), the only views between the profile and the back. charkit.geom.hull carves with them per height band when 'hull' is true, each band's azimuth and axis fitted by silhouette; off by default (see the cautions)
cautions: off for the hull ('hull': false): with the bodice and upper-skirt bands on, the build's back skirt width goes FAIL 1.995 -> PASS 0.963, but the overskirt panels drop (R 0.526 WARN -> 0.330 FAIL, L 0.451 -> 0.326) and the front skirt width 0.795 -> 0.679: the carve narrows the skirt's sides, which leave-one-out (silhouettes) doesn't see. Turn it on to re-measure once the panels are flaps (tool/body); docs/workstreams/refs2.md
not a rigid turn: the head and bodice are drawn 10-25 degrees further round than the legs, so it calibrates per band, never as one view

leave-one-out kept head, bodice, upper skirt and legs; the build drops head (the buns come out rounder: hair_piece_buns 0.686 -> 0.632) and legs (the soles carved: feet 0.05 L high); the stepped hem panels (-3.5..-2.3 L) fail leave-one-out in every candidate
no outfit masks draw these views: their pieces come from the sheet's labels voted per drawn cell (hull.extra_pieces); 'pieces': false keeps the sheet's labels
the buns are drawn rounder than the sheet's blocky loops in places; take the buns' shape from bun_detail

bun_detail.role: the buns' construction for the hair's bun template: top row the head from the buns to the chin at the sheet's four angles (front, three-quarter, profile, back; against the sheet's heads above the eye line, registered by the front's eye spacing: IoU 0.929-0.952, the buns' top 0.4 L 0.89-0.94); bottom row one bun alone from the front, the side, behind, above and three-quarter: the loop's opening, the band's thickness, its flat faces and squared corners, where it ties into the hair
cautions: the bottom row is unchecked: no sheet view draws a bun alone; the loop's construction there is the model's reading of the design (the view from above is the most schematic)
the top row is drawn about 1.86x the sheet's scale

skirt_back_sides_detail.role: the layered skirt on a mannequin, waist to knees, in six views: top row front, three-quarter, profile; bottom row three-quarter back (her left), back, three-quarter back (her right): the back and side panels, where each starts at the waist, how the steps run and how far the hem flares, for the skirt's and panels' builders
cautions: checked against the sheet's skirt (the garment classes below the waistband, scale fitted): front 0.927, three-quarter 0.844, profile 0.799, back 0.913
its three-quarter backs are unverified: 0.61 against body_turnaround_back34's, whose hem band the hull rejected; use them for construction (panel order, overlaps), not for widths
the mannequin is generic: take the skirt's length and flare on the body from the sheet

hull.role: the character's 3D shape carved from body_turnaround's calibrated orthographic views (charkit.geom.hull): the hair's source (hair.shape.glb) and the aligned 3D target in place of TRELLIS; coloured from the views, its vertices labelled with the QA's classes, its eyes known exactly (the sidecar hull.glb.json). Built where missing or stale (manifest.produced)
cautions: a visual hull: concavities no view shows are filled (the eye sockets, between the locks); the hair is one mass, not locks
limbs are carved apart from the body where the outfit's pieces say so (a cuff, a sleeve); a limb whose front run the pieces don't split still takes the body's depth

hair_layers.role: the hair's families (hair_breakdown's legend: bangs, side locks, upper and lower back, buns, ahoge, flyaways) on body_turnaround's hair, per view (front, profile, back; bodyqa.design_views grids, keys VIEW__FAMILY): the targets of the hair's pieces (charkit.geom.hairpieces). Built where missing or stale (manifest.produced)
cautions: the breakdown is another generation of the design: registered onto the body sheet at hair IoU 0.68-0.80, so only which family a body-sheet hair pixel belongs to comes from it; the body sheet is the silhouettes' authority
no three-quarter view: the hair's pieces predict it in 3D
the buns are the outfit's bun pieces (outfit_masks), not the breakdown's

outfit_truth.role: a hand-checked labelling of body_turnaround's four views by outfit piece, on the outfit masks' grids (bodyqa.design_views at the sheet's 212.5 px/L): what `python -m charkit outfit score` grades the produced masks against (outfit.score)

provenance.method: every cell of 25 px or more (outfit.cells: 263 in the four views) labelled by eye from zoomed crops beside the cells; the file's meta holds the calls

cautions: one reading by eye: where the drawing allows either (the profile's two bow tails, a tuft under a bun, the hem's pixels at the shorts' edge) a set is accepted

it takes the overskirt panels as hanging from the waistband over the skirt (Michael, 2026-09-29): the back's and the profile's unbroken cells from the waistband into the tails are the panels, which a line-art reading (one cell, one piece) shares with outfit.match_view
valid for the grids it records only: a new sheet, a new eye spacing or a new window needs it redrawn, and outfit.score refuses a grid that differs

outfit_masks.role: the outfit graph's pieces as per-view masks on body_turnaround (bodyqa.design_views grids, keys VIEW__PIECE), the graph they were cut with beside them (outfit_graph.json): the visual hull's per-piece carving and labels. Built where missing or stale (manifest.produced)
cautions: made from the rig and body_turnaround alone (outfit.sheet_field: the rig's layers laid out in 3D by the sheet's front and profile, then relabelled by the views); nothing gitignored is read. Until 2026-09-30 a TRELLIS field found in charkit/out/i3d/ext steered them, and copies without it made other masks (docs/workstreams/outfit-source.md)

scored against the hand-checked truth (outfit_truth, `python -m charkit outfit score`): 0.972 of the garment pixels agree (front 0.993, three-quarter 0.966, profile 0.909, back 0.993; mean piece IoU 0.913); the TRELLIS-steered masks scored 0.865 (0.786). The largest misses: the profile's panel side and skirt hem, the buns' undersides, the crab clip

the graph's comparison with the spec's hand list is made against the garments' and accessories' roles only (reads_spec: names, kinds, sides, bones, region bones, az), so its matches are the spec's own but it lists no knob deltas; `python -m charkit outfit SPEC` gives the full comparison
a piece a view hides has an empty mask there

notes: 2026-09-28: four generated references added (gen/). The authority map is unchanged until each is checked against the sheet; candidates: face_profile and skull -> head_construction / head_turnaround, garment piece shapes -> garment_breakdown, hair layers -> hair_breakdown.

2026-09-28 (second session): the generated sheets are the base; idol_D is the source design only. 'sheets' names which reference fills the 'sheet' role per kind (face and eyes: head_turnaround; body, hair silhouettes and palette: body_turnaround); the eyes' authority moved from the rig to it; expressions have none (the template library's). charkit refcheck: the turnarounds agree with each other; head_construction is the outlier on the chin, neck, pupil aspect and lid line, so it holds the skull and ears only.

2026-09-28: the hull (charkit.geom.hull) replaces TRELLIS as the hair's source (hair.shape.glb = ref:hull): against TRELLIS hair, 12 checks better and none worse (the buns' height PASS in every view, hair IoU front 0.49 -> 0.77). TRELLIS stays for the outfit graph's field.

2026-09-28 (Michael): the generated 3D character grades nothing: face_depth and hair_shape have no authority, so face_shape_depth and shape_iou_hair are INFO. The hull is the hair's source; its face is no face target (its rows' sections ridge across it), and the hair cut from it is measured against the sheet (body_*_hair_*, sheet_shown_*).
